attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his own Substack post. The WSJ headline is cited only as his example.

semantics.note: 'This' points back to several assertions. Narrowing it to errors and limitations follows the WSJ example he gives right after. It drops the broader 'dud' and 'scaling' points but keeps the checkable core.

contract.note: This is a plain, ordinary reading. It does not require all businesses to agree, and it reads 'finally' as growing recognition. The early-2024 window fits a statement made in June 2024.

evidence.note: McKinsey survey, fieldwork Feb–Mar 2024, published May 2024. Nearly a quarter of respondents at gen-AI adopters reported harm from inaccuracy, the most-cited risk, and attention to the risk rose. The report also notes business value.

reviews.rationale: The contract asks for evidence that businesses ran into consequential inaccuracies and increasingly recognised the limits. In the in-window survey, inaccuracy is the most-reported risk that caused negative consequences (23%), and awareness of it grew. That meets the support condition. The finding of business value does not show that inaccuracies were uncommon, so the contradiction condition is not met.

attribution.note: Marcus's own assertion in his own post.

semantics.note: It keeps 'subtle', 'mostly', 'lying or exaggerating' and 'a couple years ago'. The direction of the shift, toward long-term promises, appears in the contract rather than in the proposition, which is acceptable.

contract.note: Reading 'mostly' as a predominant pattern and 'a couple years ago' as about 2022 is fair and ordinary. The result depends on these readings because Marcus gave no sample or measure.

evidence.note: Google's 2022 company disclosure is candid about LaMDA's inaccuracies. It is one counterexample and cannot show the industry's predominant pattern.
In 2023, Altman himself distinguished short-term hype from long-term optimism. This muddies a neat timeline but does not measure how common either kind of messaging was.

reviews.rationale: Both the support and contradiction conditions require a representative comparison of 2022 and 2024 promotional claims, and the packet has none. The two items are isolated examples that cut against a clean account but cannot establish a predominant pattern or a shift. The evidence does not settle the outcome.
